h01 · the whole gang at the lens · the 1920s marble bank lobby

A frame from a 1920s period feature film on 35mm motion-picture film. The place is the marble bank lobby in the attached frame from the film: keep its marble, brass and morning light, the brass-and-glass front doors standing wide open behind. Just inside the doors six robbers stand in a tight pack on the marble, shoulders touching, rapping straight at the lens. The masks and suits are exactly as in the attached line-up card, masks copied exactly from its close-ups: PLUM, BOTTLE, CRIMSON, MARINE, RUST and SILVER. Each balaclava has a white wool ring round the face and one small red felt triangle over the man's left eye, on the right side of the picture. Black leather gloves, collars up, no skin. CRIMSON is nearest, hunched forward, knees bent, his right index finger jabbing at the lens, large and slightly soft; the others crowd in behind him, gloved palms frozen at the bottom of a downward chop. Low wide-angle 21mm from a metre away, tilted a few degrees. Behind them customers keep their hands up while an elderly doorman politely holds the door. Morning sun through the doors is the only light. 16:9.
